correctness.rationale: For a product point \((x,y)\), if the strict upper set has minimum \((a,b)\), any strict increase in \(x\) forces \(b=y\) and any strict increase in \(y\) forces \(a=x\); hence both coordinates cannot be nonmaximal. If \(y\) is maximal, the strict upper set is exactly \({(x' ,y):x'>x}\), so its having a minimum is equivalent to \(x\) being up beat; the symmetric case gives the other alternative. Passing to opposite orders proves the down-beat statement. The minimality equivalence follows by choosing maximal or minimal points in the other finite factor. Products of the core deformation retractions give a strong deformation retract onto \(C_X\times C_Y\), which is minimal by the local theorem. The bundled verifier replays 32,720 local equivalence checks and 2,281 product-minimality checks with VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: Core cardinality is the exact size of the minimal representative of a finite-space strong homotopy type. The theorem shows that this invariant is multiplicative under Cartesian products and, more strongly, gives a pointwise criterion locating every beat point of a product. It rules out hidden beat-point compression in products of minimal spaces and lets product cores be computed without running a reduction algorithm on the product. This is a natural structural fact about a central invariant, not an arbitrary finite census or parameter slice.
